description: Remote control for coding agents via Slack/Discord

phases.name: Project Setup
phases.outcome: TypeScript project builds, tests run, init script passes

features.description: Initialize npm project with package.json (name, version, bin, scripts, engines)
verification: package.json exists with name 'openbridge'
bin field points to CLI entry point
engines field requires node >= 18

features.description: Configure TypeScript (tsconfig.json with strict mode, ES2022 target, Node module resolution)
verification: tsconfig.json exists with strict: true
npx tsc --noEmit succeeds with zero errors
Output directory is dist/

features.description: Create src/ directory structure with placeholder entry point
verification: src/index.ts exists and exports a main function
npx tsc compiles successfully to dist/
node dist/index.js runs without error

features.description: Set up test framework (vitest)
verification: vitest is in devDependencies
npm test runs vitest
A placeholder test in src/__tests__/ passes

features.description: scripts/init.sh check subcommand verifies environment
verification: ./scripts/init.sh check reports Node.js version
./scripts/init.sh check reports whether claude CLI is available
./scripts/init.sh check reports whether codex CLI is available
./scripts/init.sh check verifies .env.local exists (or warns)

features.description: scripts/build.sh compiles TypeScript to dist/
verification: ./scripts/build.sh runs tsc and exits 0
dist/ directory contains compiled JS files

features.description: scripts/test.sh runs the test suite
verification: ./scripts/test.sh runs vitest and exits 0
Placeholder test passes

features.description: .gitignore covers node_modules, dist, .env.local, .openbridge/, OS files
verification: git status does not show node_modules or dist
.env.local is ignored
.openbridge/ is ignored

features.description: .env.example documents all required environment variables
verification: .env.example exists with placeholder values for SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_APP_TOKEN, DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN
Comments explain what each variable is for

phases.name: Normalized Event Types and Backend Interface
phases.outcome: Shared types and backend contract defined, both backends parse real CLI output

features.description: Define normalized event types as TypeScript interfaces (AssistantText, ToolUse, ToolResult, CommandExecution, PermissionDenied, SessionStarted, TurnCompleted, Error)
verification: src/types/events.ts exports all event type interfaces
Each event type has a discriminant 'type' field
PermissionDenied includes toolName, toolInput, and context fields
TypeScript compiles with no errors

features.description: Define backend interface (start, send, getSessionId, stop) as TypeScript interface
verification: src/types/backend.ts exports Backend interface
send() returns Promise<{ events: NormalizedEvent[], sessionId: string | null }>
TypeScript compiles with no errors

features.description: Claude Code backend — spawn oneshot process and collect stdout
verification: src/backends/claude.ts implements Backend interface
send() spawns 'claude -p --verbose --output-format stream-json --input-format text'
Process stdout is collected as a string
Process exits and exit code is captured

features.description: Claude Code backend — parse session_id from system init event
verification: First send() extracts session_id from the system init event
getSessionId() returns the extracted session_id
Unit test with sample system init JSON verifies extraction

features.description: Claude Code backend — parse assistant text from assistant events
verification: Text content from assistant message.content[] is extracted
Multiple text blocks are concatenated
Returns AssistantText normalized events
Unit test with sample assistant JSON verifies parsing

features.description: Claude Code backend — parse permission_denials from result event
verification: permission_denials array from result event is parsed
Each denial produces a PermissionDenied normalized event with toolName and toolInput
Empty permission_denials array produces no PermissionDenied events
Unit test with sample result JSON verifies parsing

features.description: Claude Code backend — parse permission context from user error events
verification: user events with is_error: true are scanned for permission-related text
Context text is included in PermissionDenied events
Unit test verifies extraction

features.description: Claude Code backend — parse error events
verification: result events with is_error: true produce Error normalized events
Non-zero exit codes with no structured error produce Error events
Unit test verifies both cases

features.description: Claude Code backend — session resume with -r flag
verification: Second send() call includes -r SESSION_ID in args
Session ID from first call is reused
Unit test verifies args construction for resume

features.description: Codex CLI backend — spawn oneshot process and collect stdout
verification: src/backends/codex.ts implements Backend interface
send() spawns 'codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --json'
Process stdout is collected as a string
Process exits and exit code is captured

features.description: Codex CLI backend — parse thread_id from thread.started event
verification: First send() extracts thread_id from thread.started event
getSessionId() returns the extracted thread_id
Unit test with sample thread.started JSON verifies extraction

features.description: Codex CLI backend — parse agent_message text
verification: item.completed events with type agent_message are parsed
Text content is extracted as AssistantText normalized events
Unit test verifies parsing

features.description: Codex CLI backend — parse command_execution events
verification: item.completed events with type command_execution are parsed
exit_code and aggregated_output are captured as CommandExecution events
Unit test verifies parsing

features.description: Codex CLI backend — detect sandbox denial patterns in output
verification: Agent message text matching /operation not permitted|permission denied/i produces PermissionDenied events
Command execution output with these patterns also detected
Unit test with sample sandbox denial output verifies detection

features.description: Codex CLI backend — session resume with resume subcommand
verification: Second send() uses 'codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check --json SESSION_ID'
--sandbox flag is NOT included in resume args
Unit test verifies args construction for resume

features.description: Codex CLI backend — configurable sandbox mode
verification: Backend accepts sandbox option (workspace-write, read-only, danger-full-access)
sandbox flag is included in initial startArgs only
Default is workspace-write
Unit test verifies startArgs include --sandbox

phases.name: SQLite Persistence and Router
phases.outcome: Bridge state persists across restarts, router maps channels to projects and sessions

features.description: SQLite store — initialize database with WAL mode in .openbridge/ directory
verification: src/store.ts creates .openbridge/bridge.db if it doesn't exist
Database is opened with WAL journal mode
Unit test verifies database file is created

features.description: SQLite store — projects table schema (id, channel_id, project_dir, backend_name, created_at)
verification: projects table is created on init
channel_id has a unique index
Unit test verifies table creation

features.description: SQLite store — sessions table schema (id, thread_id, project_id, backend_session_id, state, created_at, updated_at)
verification: sessions table is created on init
thread_id has a unique index
state defaults to 'idle'
Unit test verifies table creation

features.description: SQLite store — settings table schema (key, value)
verification: settings table is created on init
key is the primary key
Unit test verifies table creation

features.description: SQLite store — schema migrations via version table
verification: schema_version table tracks current version
Migrations run sequentially on startup
Re-running init does not duplicate tables
Unit test verifies idempotent initialization

features.description: SQLite store — CRUD for projects (create, getByChannelId, list, delete)
verification: createProject inserts a row and returns it
getProjectByChannelId retrieves by channel_id
listProjects returns all projects
deleteProject removes by id
Unit tests verify all four operations

features.description: SQLite store — CRUD for sessions (create, getByThreadId, updateState, updateSessionId, delete)
verification: createSession inserts with state 'idle'
getSessionByThreadId retrieves by thread_id
updateSessionState changes state field and updated_at
updateBackendSessionId sets backend_session_id for resume
Unit tests verify all operations

features.description: SQLite store — CRUD for settings (get, set, delete)
verification: setSetting upserts a key-value pair
getSetting retrieves value by key, returns null if missing
deleteSetting removes by key
Unit tests verify all operations

features.description: Session state machine — valid transitions enforced
verification: idle → running (on send)
running → idle (on turn complete)
running → waiting_for_input (on permission denied)
waiting_for_input → running (on user response)
running → dead (on crash/timeout)
dead → idle (on restart)
Invalid transitions throw an error
Unit tests verify all valid and invalid transitions

features.description: Router — resolve channel + thread to project and backend
verification: Given a channel_id and thread_id, router returns project config and session state
Unknown channel_id returns null (message is not for a bound project)
Unit test verifies resolution

features.description: Router — create new session for unknown thread in bound channel
verification: First message in a new thread creates a session row in SQLite
Session state starts as idle
Router returns the new session
Unit test verifies session creation

features.description: Router — send message through backend and return normalized events
verification: Router calls backend.send() with the message text
Session state transitions to running during send, back to idle on completion
Backend session_id is stored in SQLite for resume
Normalized events are returned to the caller
Unit test with mock backend verifies the flow

features.description: Router — detect permission denial and transition to waiting_for_input
verification: When send() returns PermissionDenied events, session state becomes waiting_for_input
Router returns the PermissionDenied events to the caller for rendering
Unit test with mock backend returning PermissionDenied verifies state transition

features.description: Router — handle user response when waiting_for_input
verification: When session is waiting_for_input, next message is routed as a resume
Session transitions from waiting_for_input → running → idle
Unit test verifies the resume flow

features.description: Router — reset session (/new command)
verification: Reset clears the backend_session_id in SQLite
Next message starts a fresh session (no -r flag)
Session state returns to idle
Unit test verifies reset

phases.name: Slack Adapter
phases.outcome: Users can message the bot in Slack and get responses from the coding backend

features.description: Slack app connects via Socket Mode using @slack/bolt
verification: src/adapters/slack.ts creates a Bolt app with Socket Mode
App connects successfully with valid SLACK_BOT_TOKEN and SLACK_APP_TOKEN
Connection logged on startup

features.description: Slack adapter implements shared adapter interface
verification: src/types/adapter.ts defines Adapter interface (start, stop, postMessage, postInteractive, postError)
Slack adapter implements this interface
TypeScript compiles with no errors

features.description: Slack — listen for messages in bound channels and route to router
verification: Messages in channels with bound projects are passed to the router
Messages in unbound channels are ignored
Bot's own messages are ignored (no loops)

features.description: Slack — auto-move top-level channel messages into new threads
verification: Message sent directly in channel (not in thread) triggers bot to create a new thread
Bot replies in the new thread, not in the channel
Channel stays clean — only thread starters visible

features.description: Slack — route thread messages to correct session
verification: Messages in a thread are routed to the session mapped to that thread
Different threads in the same channel go to different sessions
New thread creates a new session automatically

features.description: Slack — post assistant text responses back to thread
verification: AssistantText events are posted as Slack messages in the originating thread
Long responses are not truncated (Slack's limit is ~4000 chars per message)
Responses longer than limit are split into multiple messages

features.description: Slack — render permission denial as Block Kit interactive message
verification: PermissionDenied events render as a Slack message with tool name and input
Message includes Allow and Deny buttons
Message includes text: 'or type a custom response'
Buttons use Block Kit actions layout

features.description: Slack — handle Allow button click on permission prompt
verification: Clicking Allow sends the appropriate response to the router
Router resumes the backend session
Button message is updated to show the selection (ephemeral or edit)
Session transitions from waiting_for_input → running → idle

features.description: Slack — handle Deny button click on permission prompt
verification: Clicking Deny sends denial to the router
Backend session is informed of denial
Button message is updated to show denial was selected

features.description: Slack — handle freeform text as custom response when waiting_for_input
verification: When session is waiting_for_input, a typed message is treated as the custom response
Text is passed to router as the user's reply
Session resumes with the custom text

features.description: Slack — post error messages for backend failures
verification: Error normalized events are posted as Slack messages with clear explanation
Backend crash posts a message explaining what happened
Message includes suggested fix when possible

features.description: Slack — register /project slash command
verification: /project is registered in Slack app manifest
Command handler routes to project creation flow
TypeScript compiles with handler registered

features.description: Slack — /project with name creates new channel and binds it
verification: /project my-app from a bound channel creates #my-app channel
New channel is bound to a project directory
Confirmation message posted

features.description: Slack — /project from unbound channel offers bind options
verification: /project from unbound channel shows 'Use this channel' and 'Create new' buttons
User selection binds the channel appropriately

features.description: Slack — /project with no args lists all bindings
verification: /project with no args lists all channel → project → backend bindings
Unbound project directories are also listed
User can select one to link

features.description: Slack — /new resets session in current thread
verification: /new in a thread resets the backend session
Next message starts a fresh conversation
Confirmation message posted in thread

features.description: Slack — /settings displays and modifies bridge configuration
verification: /settings shows current backend, project directory
User can change backend for the current project
Changes are persisted to SQLite

features.description: Slack — file upload handling
verification: File attachment in a project thread is downloaded from Slack
File is saved to the project directory (or temp location)
File path is included in the message sent to the backend
Backend receives context about the uploaded file

features.description: Discord — handle freeform text when waiting_for_input

features.description: Discord — post error messages

features.description: Discord — register slash commands (/project, /new, /settings)

features.description: Discord — /project command flow (create, list, bind)
verification: /project name creates channel and binds
/project with no args lists bindings

features.description: Discord — /new resets session

Confirmation posted

features.description: Discord — /settings command

npm install -g . makes 'openbridge' available globally
openbridge --help shows usage

features.description: openbridge init — backend auto-detection
verification: Checks if claude CLI is available on PATH
Checks if codex CLI is available on PATH
Reports which backends were found
User can select default backend

features.description: openbridge init — first project creation
verification: Prompts for project name and directory path
Creates project entry in SQLite
Reports that project is ready

features.description: openbridge init — writes config to .openbridge/
verification: .openbridge/ directory is created

phases.name: Integration and Polish
phases.outcome: Full end-to-end flow works reliably, graceful error handling throughout

features.description: End-to-end: Slack message → Claude Code → response posted in thread
verification: Send message in bound Slack channel
Claude Code processes it and responds
Response appears in the Slack thread
Session ID is stored for resume

features.description: End-to-end: Slack permission denial → buttons → Allow → resume
verification: Claude Code hits permission boundary
Slack shows interactive message with Allow/Deny buttons
User clicks Allow
Backend resumes and completes the task

features.description: End-to-end: Slack permission denial → freeform text → resume
verification: Claude Code hits permission boundary
Slack shows permission prompt
User types a custom response instead of clicking buttons
Backend resumes with the custom text

features.description: End-to-end: Discord message → Codex CLI → response
verification: Send message in bound Discord channel
Codex CLI processes it and responds
Response appears in Discord thread

features.description: Session persistence across bridge restart
verification: Start a session, send a message, get response
Restart the bridge process
Send another message in the same thread
Backend resumes the previous session (session_id retrieved from SQLite)

features.description: Graceful shutdown — stop all backends, close connections
verification: SIGTERM triggers graceful shutdown
All active backend sessions are stopped
Messaging platform connections are closed
Process exits cleanly

features.description: Error handling — missing CLI tool reported to user
verification: If claude CLI is not found, error message posted in thread
If codex CLI is not found, error message posted in thread
Message includes suggested fix (install instructions)

features.description: Error handling — backend timeout reported to user
verification: If backend takes longer than configurable timeout, session is killed
Error message posted in thread explaining timeout
Session state transitions to dead

features.description: Error handling — backend crash reported to user
verification: If backend process crashes (non-zero exit, signal), error is caught
Error message posted in thread with exit code/signal
Session state transitions to dead
Next message in thread starts fresh session

features.description: Logging — consistent prefixes for all bridge components
verification: All log lines include component prefix (e.g., [slack], [router], [claude], [store])
Log levels used appropriately (info, warn, error)
Startup logs show which platforms and backends are active
